name: OT-2 hydrogel pipetting-and-imaging platform (Nazeri et al., HardwareX 2025)
brief: A liquid handling robot with a deck of well plates and vials runs combinatorial, high-throughput soft-materials synthesis (ionically crosslinked hydrogels): it pipettes reagents and a USB camera mounted on the gantry tool adapter images the crosslinking in situ over time without manual transfer.

cost.original: Cost of hardware: $10,000 USD (OT-2) + $110 USD (Hardware Module); BOM sums to $10,109.23
cost.excludes_note: Pipettes, tips, labware, PC, consumables and chemicals not itemised; the OT-2 price is the authors' quoted $10,000 (LabX), not a list price.

notes: price_basis=base, set from the source wording ("$10,000 USD (OT-2)": the bare robot) before base/configured catalog prices were researched. OT-2 is 98.9% of the BOM value; the camera and printed parts are not in the catalog. Opened the PMC full text (Europe PMC XML) 3 Oct 2026. Specifications table: "Cost of hardware $10,000 USD (OT-2) + $110 USD (Hardware Module)". BOM table: Opentrons OT-2 1 x $10,000 (LabX); Opti-Tekscope OT-HD camera $88.08; 3D-printed PLA part $18.99; 3 stainless screws $2.16. Mapped fraction: 1 of 4 BOM lines (the OT-2) maps to catalog id opentrons_ot2 but it is 98.9% of the stated value ($10,000 of $10,109); the rest is a USB camera, a printed part and screws with no catalog id (the camera/adapter are the paper's contribution, so this is an OT-2 price check with an add-on). Weak as a whole-lab test (single instrument, author-quoted price).
